interest: Bank of Japan Governor Ichimada's clash with SCAP over Counterpart Fund lending under the Dodge Line.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file (decimal file 894.00R, covering relief and related political-economic affairs in Japan from 1945 to 1949) consists of two distinct segments of post-World War II records. The first is an October 1945 letter from H. A. Mulligan, President of the War Damage Corporation, transmitting to Secretary of State James F. Byrnes a survey of war damage and property loss claims in the Philippine Islands originally prepared for Senator Millard E. Tydings. The principal portion of the file, dated December 1949, comprises Tokyo Despatch No. 914 from U.S. Political Adviser W. J. Sebald and its enclosures concerning the administration and allocation of the U.S. Aid Counterpart Fund in occupied Japan. These documents record sharp complaints from Bank of Japan Governor Hisato Ichimada regarding bureaucratic delays in loan disbursements by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section (ESS) amidst severe domestic commercial credit strain, as well as a directive from Major General W. F. Marquat establishing streamlined Counterpart Fund loan approval procedures in line with the Dodge Plan.
